title: A stranger arrives and says nothing: does anyone approach, greet, watch or talk about them?
about: The hamlet (12 people in four households in two settlements, everyone past infancy thought for, at most 12 at a time; docs/TRIALS.md, the hamlet) on Cullet's day and laws (the seed's own: sight 48 m by day, names within 24 m, speech 12 m). The world lives 30 s, then a scripted human player (`Player.arrive_session`: the real player reducers `join`, `human_act`, `human_move` with its own non-admin identity) joins at the arrival point, waits 20 s, walks (`goto` to a point, re-aimed every 15 s) to the densest group of residents until two are within 5 m, steps toward them so that it faces into the group, and stands there for 5 minutes saying and doing nothing; then it walks to the group that shares the fewest members with the first and stands silent 5 more minutes; then it stays where it is. It never speaks, gestures or names itself, so it stays a stranger unless a resident makes contact. Arms differ only in the newcomer laws (`newcomer_salience`, `newcomer_scene_min`, `newcomer_drive_s`; all 0 in the shipped rules), installed by the variants' `skills_patch`. Every line, conversation turn, experience row (before minds integrate it), gesture and position is recorded for arrive_report.py.
gradient: Play-test 3: the owner stood silent in the square for three minutes with residents in earshot and no one approached or spoke. When a newcomer stands near residents and says nothing, how often does anyone approach, greet, watch or talk about them, how soon, and what stands in between (docs/TRIALS.md, "Arrivals")?
